papers.abstract: To each ternary sextic $f(X_0, X_1, X_2)$ whose associated plane curve is smooth, the Shioda construction attaches a smooth sextic fourfold $X \subset \mathbb{P}^5$ whose defining equation $f(X_0, X_1, X_2) - f(Y_0, Y_1, Y_2)$ is fixed under the involution $ι: (X_0, X_1, X_2, Y_0, Y_1, Y_2) \mapsto i \cdot (Y_0, Y_1, Y_2, -X_0, -X_1, -X_2)$. The induced action $ι^* : H^4(X, \mathbb{Q}) \to H^4(X, \mathbb{Q})$ fixes a Hodge substructure $H \subset H^4(X, \mathbb{Q})$ whose Hodge coniveau is 1. By the general Hodge conjecture, we expect that there should exist a divisor $Y \subset X$ for which $H \subset \ker\left( H^4(X, \mathbb{Q}) \to H^4(X \setminus Y, \mathbb{Q}) \right)$. We verify this prediction in case the Waring rank of $f(X_0, X_1, X_2)$ takes on its minimum possible value, partially answering a question of Voisin (J. Math. Sci. Univ. Tokyo '15).

papers.name: A rational model for the fiberwise THH transfer I: Sullivan algebras
papers.abstract: Given a map $f$ of fibrations over a space $B$ such that the fiber of $f$ is simply connected and finitely dominated, we prove that its fiberwise THH transfer, considered as a map of parametrized spectra over $B$, is rationally modeled by the Hochschild homology transfer of a Sullivan model of $f$. The proof goes in two steps. Firstly, we use the machinery of higher categorical traces to show that the fiberwise THH transfer can be computed internally to parametrized spectra. Secondly, we model the resulting description rationally using work of Braunack-Mayer, who proved that parametrized spectra can be modeled by modules over Sullivan algebras. In Part II, we will use our result to obtain a rational model of the Becker-Gottlieb transfer, and for applications to manifold topology.

papers.name: The SK model with a sparse variance profile: free energy and AMP-based magnetization estimation at high temperature
papers.abstract: A generalization of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model for spin glasses is considered, in which the interaction matrix is endowed with a variance profile that has no particular structure and may be sparse. In the first part of the paper, an asymptotic equivalent of the free energy is derived at sufficiently high temperatures, regardless of the signature of the variance profile matrix. In the second part, the mean of the spin vector under the Gibbs measure is estimated using an Approximate Message Passing algorithm that generalizes the one used for the SK case. The dynamical approach of Adhikari et al (J Stat Phys 2021), originally developed for the classical SK model, is adapted to the present setting to obtain these results.

papers.name: Proof of Dittert's conjecture for dimensions $n\ge 17$
papers.abstract: Dittert's conjecture gives a sharp upper bound for the Dittert functional on nonnegative matrices whose entries sum to $n$. It extends the van der Waerden permanent problem from the doubly stochastic polytope to a larger simplex in which row and column sums are allowed to vary. We prove the conjecture for every dimension $n\ge 17$. The proof combines the Knopp--Sinkhorn lower bound for boundary points of the doubly stochastic polytope with a refined scaling step in the Cheon--Wanless method. The main improvement is a subset-sum estimate for the row and column sums of a near maximizer that is sharper for subset sizes in the central range and reduces the scaling factor needed to obtain a doubly superstochastic matrix. This strengthened comparison is sufficient to exclude boundary maximizers in all dimensions $n\ge 17$, and the known positive-support characterization then identifies the unique maximizer as $n^{-1}J_n$.

papers.name: Express Language Modeling
papers.abstract: We introduce a new tool, Express, for converting a non-causal attention approximation into a causal approximation with matching approximation guarantees. When combined with the state-of-the-art Thinformer approximation, Express improves upon the best known causal attention guarantees, delivering $\log^{3/2}(n)/s$ approximation error with only $O(s)$ memory and $O(s^2 \log^2(n))$ compression overhead for a sequence of length $n$. We pair these developments with an efficient I/O-aware Triton implementation, demonstrate substantial speedups over FlashAttention 2, and use Express to overcome four resource bottlenecks in the language modeling pipeline: long-context prefill, KV cache compression, long-form memory-constrained decoding, and long-form compute-constrained decoding.

papers.name: An annihilation-number Caro-Wei bound: a TxGraffiti conjecture and an independence-number bracket
papers.abstract: Computable independence bounds give intervals that can be compared by containment or by their worst-case endpoint ratios. For positive maximum degree $Δ$, the Caro-Wei sum $W$ bounds the independence number from below, while $(Δ+1)W/2$ bounds it from above. A second interval has the Havel-Hakimi residue as its lower endpoint and the annihilation number as its upper endpoint. This note proves that the annihilation number does not exceed the Caro-Wei upper endpoint. This upper bound is sharp, with equality for regular graphs of positive degree and even order. Since the residue is at least $W$, this upper bound places the residue-annihilation interval inside the Caro-Wei interval. Both endpoints can improve strictly on one graph, although the sharp worst-case endpoint ratio remains unchanged, even for connected graphs. The annihilation-number bound also proves a conjectured lower estimate based on the annihilation number and residue for every connected graph with at least three vertices. Equality in this estimate holds for exactly eight graph types, while the single edge violates it. For maximum degree at least three, however, the estimate never exceeds the residue, even without connectedness.

papers.name: Machine learning the arithmetic of Boyd's Mahler measure conjectures
papers.abstract: Boyd conjectured that the Mahler measure of $P_k(x,y)=x+y+\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}+k$ for $k$ an integer, is given by $r_kL'(E_k,0)$, where $E_k$ is the elliptic curve associated to the zero locus of $P_k$ and $r_k$ is a rational number. We study various arithmetic properties of $r_k$ using a dataset containing the first $250{,}000$ values of $k$, combining large-scale statistical analysis assisted by \textsc{Claude} with transformer-based experiments carried out using Axolver. We recover Boyd's observation that, apart from a few exceptions, $r_k$ is the reciprocal of an integer. The size of this integer is governed by the conductor of the elliptic curve. Moreover, its $p$-adic valuations display markedly different behavior according to the prime. For $p\geq5$, the observed frequencies of $v_p(r_k)=-m$, for $m\geq1$, are close to $p^{-m}$. At $p=5$, the agreement improves substantially when we restrict to curves with good reduction at $5$. For the primes $2$ and $3$, however, we find additional arithmetic structure involving congruence conditions on $k$ and the primes of bad reduction of $E_k$. Although the neural networks do not predict $r_k$ exactly, they recover significant information about its magnitude and valuations. In particular, the experiments at the prime $2$ suggest predictive relationships within the computed range that are not fully captured by the explicit predictor obtained from our statistical analysis.

papers.name: Kusner's conjecture on equilateral sets is false
papers.abstract: We disprove Kusner's 1983 conjecture that every equilateral set in $\ell_p^n$ with $2<p<\infty$ has at most $n+1$ points: there exist $58$ points in $\mathbb{R}^{56}$ whose pairwise $\ell_5$ distances are all equal, so the maximum equilateral-set size satisfies $e(\ell_5^{56})\ge58>57$. This is the first equilateral set of more than $n+1$ points in $\ell_p^n$ for any finite $p\ge2$. The construction persists on an open interval of exponents around $5$. The configuration is specified by the unique solution of an explicit polynomial system with rational coefficients in a rational box; existence and uniqueness are proved by exact integer inequalities. The existence of the $58$-point equilateral set in $\ell_5^{56}$ has been formalised in Lean from standard axioms.

papers.name: The Brualdi--Hoffman--Turán problem for odd wheels: Resolving a conjecture of Yu, Li and Peng
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the Brualdi--Hoffman--Turán problem, which asks for the maximum adjacency spectral radius over graphs with a fixed number of edges that forbid a prescribed subgraph. We settle an open conjecture due to Yu, Li and Peng for odd wheel graphs $W_{2k+1}$. A striking dichotomy appears in the extremal configurations: the forbidden-$W_5$ case and the general case $k\ge 3$ rely on identical stability and dense-core reductions but produce completely different extremal graphs. For sufficiently large size $m$, we derive sharp spectral inequalities and give complete characterizations for graphs achieving equality. Our approach combines the edge-spectral stability theorem with the dense-core method and residual-function analysis. Beyond solving the target conjecture, the developed framework provides a systematic approach for edge-spectral Turán problems and implies several known results for odd cycles, friendship graphs and odd fans. Directions for future research on edge-spectral supersaturation are also discussed.

papers.name: On Samuels' Conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $0\leqμ_1\leq\cdots\leqμ_n$ and let $λ>\sum_{i=1}^nμ_i$. Let $X_1,...,X_n$ be independent nonnegative random variables satisfying $\mathbb{E}X_i=μ_i$, and write $D_i := λ-\sum_{k=1}^{i-1}μ_k$ for $1\leq i\leq n$. We prove that $$ \inf_{X_1,...,X_n} \mathbb{P}\left( \sum_{i=1}^nX_i<λ\right) = \min_{1\leq i\leq n} \prod_{j=i}^n \left( 1-\frac{μ_j}{D_i} \right). $$ The bound is sharp and is attained. This proves Samuels' conjecture. Feige's conjecture is thereby resolved, since it follows immediately from the equal-means case. The proof is self-contained.

papers.name: The least-squares RBF-PU method for linear elasticity in the diaphragm geometry
papers.abstract: The human diaphragm is vital for respiration and its simulation can aid in further understanding complications arising in individuals that have been subjected to mechanical ventilation. The diaphragm is very thin and hence its numerical simulation poses a challenge for most numerical methods. In this paper, we compute the deformation of real diaphragm geometries, which are modelled as linearly elastic, and are subject to realistic boundary conditions. The method used is the unfitted least-squares radial basis function partition of unity method. The patches used are cylindrical and refinement is performed along the thin direction of the diaphragm. Both the unfitted nature of the method as well as the refinement technique make this method particularly well suited to solve problems formulated in thin geometries. We derive a theoretical proof showing that the method converges with high order to the solution of a well-posed linear elasticity boundary value problem.

papers.name: Transverse Analytic Envelopes and the Baum--Bott Rationality Conjecture
papers.abstract: We study holomorphic first integrals near singular leaves through transverse analytic envelopes. For diagonal actions these are normal toric quotients, and complete semiglobal integrability along singular orbits with independent support weights is equivalent to maximal resonance rank and finite monodromy. For commuting fields in convergent simultaneous Poincaré--Dulac normal form, induced derivations determine the first-integral algebra. Labelled quotients and logarithmic residues reconstruct weights at maximal rank; Grassmannians describe the ambiguity otherwise. Polynomial examples show losses invisible to prescribed finite jets. For the Baum--Bott rationality conjecture, we prove rationality and an explicit residue formula for smooth compact singular components with product charts and a common invertible semisimple transverse linear part of maximal resonance rank. Equivariant cohomology gives higher-degree vanishing for affine diagonal torus actions, including intersecting singular strata.

papers.name: Open Inextensible Filaments in Planar Stokes Flow: Well-Posedness, Endpoint Asymptotics, and Straightening
papers.abstract: We study an inextensible open filament with free ends in a planar Stokes fluid. The system reduces to a third-order nonlocal curvature equation coupled to an elliptic equation for the tension. We prove local well-posedness for nearly critical initial data in supported Sobolev spaces $\widetilde H^s$, $-1/2<s\le0$, satisfying the arc-chord condition. For positive times, we prove improved Sobolev regularity and derive a $d^{3/2}$-type expansion at each free end using Wiener--Hopf factorization, where $d$ denotes the distance to that endpoint. We further prove global existence and exponential convergence to a straight filament for sufficiently small initial data and for finite-energy initial data satisfying $E(0)<π^2/4$. The finite-energy result follows from an energy identity and a geometric estimate relating the bending energy to the arc-chord constant. More generally, any finite-time breakdown must be accompanied by loss of the arc-chord condition, while every global solution either converges exponentially to a straight filament or has arc-chord constants tending to zero along a sequence of times tending to infinity.

papers.name: Proof of the singularity conjecture for discrete subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$
papers.abstract: Let $μ$ be a finitely supported probability measure on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ whose support generates a Zariski-dense discrete subgroup. We prove that its stationary probability measure on $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{R})$ is singular with respect to the $\mathrm{SO}(2)$-invariant probability measure. The proof compares winding variances on finite covers of a closed hyperbolic surface and uses a topological obstruction.

papers.name: An Equivariant Landweber Exact Functor Theorem for Abelian Compact Lie Groups
papers.abstract: We prove an equivariant Landweber exact functor theorem for abelian compact Lie groups $G$. For a graded module $N$ over the $G$-equivariant Lazard ring $L_G$, we give necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions on $N$ for the functor \[ X\longmapsto (MU_G)_*(X)\otimes_{L_G} N \] to define a homology theory on the category $\mathrm{Sp}^G$ of genuine $G$-spectra. Our criterion is obtained by varifying the Landweber exactness on each stratum indexed by a closed subgroup of $G$ and then gluing the local flatness data via Euler classes. As an application, we show that for any non-equivariant Landweber exact ring spectrum $E$, $MU_G\wedge_{MU} E$ is equivariantly Landweber exact, thereby proving a conjecture of Wisdom. Finally, we study the $G$-equivariant formal groups $\widehat E_G$ over $\hom(G^*,E)$ associated to elliptic curves $E/S$. We prove that its classifying map $\hom(G^*,E)\to\mathcal M_{\mathrm{FG}}^G$ is flat whenever $S\to\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ell}}$ is flat, and recover $\widehat E_G$ from Gepner-Meier's equivariant elliptic cohomology associated to any oriented spectral lifting of $E/S$.

papers.name: Range Failure, Resolvent Growth, and Resonance in Partially Dissipative Systems
papers.abstract: We analyze resonance for partially dissipative systems, $\dot u=Au+f(t)$, where $A$ generates a strongly stable semigroup $S(t)$ on a Hilbert space $H$. {Resonance is} the phenomenon whereby a bounded, time-periodic $f$ yields an unbounded $u$, classically occurring when $A$ has imaginary eigenvalues. In infinite dimensions, however, several other resonance notions, introduced here, may occur. Classically, {$T$-periodic solvability} is equivalent to a range condition: $\mathcal{R}(I-S(T))=H$. We describe a hierarchy of range failures, and demonstrate how the growth rate of~$||(A-iωI)^{-1}||_H$ dictates a regularity gap between $u$ and $f$. For super-polynomial growth, that gap can be infinite. We demonstrate this phenomenon and its equivalence to the existence of smooth resonant forces. The theory is motivated by a well-studied hyperbolic-parabolic system, which is a simplification of fluid-solid interactions. Our main result shows that, for a carefully constructed geometry, the PDE system exhibits smooth-forcing resonance for a dense set of periods. The geometry sharply violates geometric conditions for which finite regularity losses were shown previously.

papers.name: Reduction of Zieve's Conjecture on the Hurwitz problem to Three Branch Points
papers.abstract: M. E. Zieve conjectured that a candidate datum over the sphere is realizable whenever the gcd of the parts of every branch partition is one and it satisfies the lcm condition. We prove that this conjecture reduces to its three-branch-point case. More precisely, if every Zieve-admissible triple is realizable, then every Zieve-admissible datum with at least four branch points is realizable. As already noted by Petronio, Zieve's conjecture would imply the prime-degree conjecture of Edmonds, Kulkarni, and Stong. Song, Wen, and Zhang proved the latter conjecture in a preprint posted on arXiv in September.

papers.name: Stopping models closed under pgf composition, and the stability of randomly stopped model extensions
papers.abstract: Statistical model transformations based on randomly stopped sums, maxima, and minima are widely used to extend statistical models by introducing an additional parameter. We characterize the finite-dimensional positive stopping models for which these randomly stopped sum and extreme transformations act as statistically stable (idempotent) model extensions. Stability requires the underlying stopping model to be closed under pgf composition. We prove that any finite-dimensional, connected, positive stopping model closed under pgf composition necessarily forms a family of random variables whose pgfs commute. Using the associated Koenigs function, we establish that these models form a statistical manifold admitting a global, one-dimensional parametrization $θ= \Pr(N=1) \in (0, θ_*]$, in which the probability mass at $i$ is a polynomial in $θ$ of degree at most $i$. Within this class, we further establish a duality between those models containing the identity variable (the ones yielding statistically stable extensions) and the set of all probability distributions supported on the positive integers. By providing numerous examples of stopping models closed under pgf composition, we clarify the assertion that, under certain conditions, the only stopping model that is so is geometric.

papers.name: Zong's problem on $2d$ half-spaces containing the unit ball
papers.abstract: We prove that the intersection of $2d$ half-spaces containing the Euclidean unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a point of norm at least $\sqrt{d}$. Equality in the radius bound characterizes the cube up to orthogonal transformations. The proof gives a lower bound for the average squared norm of the vertices, weighted by the Gaussian measures of their normal cones. This estimate follows from an inequality for the Gaussian measures of a simplicial cone and its projected facets, which in turn reduces to a linear estimate for the Gaussian centroid of a simplicial cone. We also discuss a quadratic extension of the problem and give a bound for it using an independent spectral argument. This bound implies that the intersection of any $m > d$ half-spaces containing the unit ball contains a point of norm at least $\sqrt{m}\,\ln\frac{m}{m-d}$.

papers.name: Ahlfors--Weill Extension, Asymptotically Conformal Curves and Epstein--Poincaré Surfaces
papers.abstract: The Ahlfors--Weill construction explicitly extends a univalent function $f$ with Schwarzian norm less than $1/2$ to a quasiconformal homeomorphism of the Riemann sphere, an extension that can be understood geometrically through Epstein surfaces. For asymptotically conformal curves, the uniformization map can be extended to a larger disk, and Loewner theory can be used to verify that this extension is quasiconformal. In this paper, we construct a local quasireflection with such an extension. Using this local quasireflection, we modify classical estimates of Ahlfors and show that domains bounded by asymptotically conformal curves have asymptotically similar hyperbolic and quasihyperbolic metrics. Furthermore, by combining these estimates with a geometric reinterpretation of the extension through Epstein surfaces, we show that the Epstein-Poincaré surfaces of the complementary domains are arbitrarily close to one another near the curve.

papers.name: A Faithful Action of the Mapping Class Group $\mathrm{Mod}(S_g)$ on the $(2g-1)$-Sphere
papers.abstract: We prove that $\mathrm{Mod}(S_g)$ acts faithfully by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms on a $(2g-1)$-sphere when $g \geq 3$ using equivariant blow-up and bi-orderability of the Torelli group.

papers.name: Tiling 3D Space by (Translates of) a Single Polycube is Undecidable
papers.abstract: We prove co-RE-completeness, and thus undecidability, of the following problem: given a single (connected) polycube, decide whether it tiles 3D Euclidean space by translations. The same result holds if we also allow rotations and/or reflections. We reduce from Wang tiling using the decorated two-prime Sudoku construction of Greenfeld and Tao and a cyclic encoding adapted from OpenAI's 3D aperiodic tile, and apply a reduction of Kim to make the prototile connected (via faces). Dimension three is optimal: translational monotiling is known to be decidable in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ and for a single (possibly disconnected) polyomino in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

papers.name: Gaussian Fluctuations of the Gradient of the Fréchet Function and Nonstandard Asymptotics of Sample Fréchet Means
papers.abstract: We establish a central limit theorem for the gradient of the Fréchet function in local Euclidean coordinates on a metric space. Assuming a unique population mean, a consistent measurable sequence of sample means, semiconcavity or semiconvexity and moment bounds for the squared distance functions, and local $C^{1,α}$ regularity of the population Fréchet function, we prove an asymptotic linear representation for its gradient at the sample mean. The leading term is the negative empirical average of the gradients of the squared distance functions at the population mean; these gradients exist almost surely under our assumptions. On complete connected Riemannian manifolds, uniqueness of the population mean, existence of a $(2+η)$-moment, and local $C^{1,α}$ regularity suffice, and the leading term is expressed through the logarithm map. We also give a sufficient condition for the regularity of the population Fréchet function through probability bounds for neighborhoods of cut loci. We then show how the local behavior of the population Fréchet function transforms these Gaussian fluctuations into limit distributions for suitably rescaled sample Fréchet means, allowing for anisotropic scaling and non-Gaussian limits. A flat-torus example exhibits anisotropic scaling, and two examples on the circle illustrate logarithmic smeariness and the failure of any deterministic linear scaling to yield a nondegenerate limit, respectively.

papers.name: Indecomposability of derived categories and nef canonical divisors in dimensions three and four
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth projective threefold or fourfold whose bounded derived category admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition has nef canonical divisor, which establishes \cite[Conjecture~1.1]{KO2018} in these dimensions. The proof combines the classification of extremal contractions with constructions of nontrivial admissible subcategories. In dimension four, we refine the descriptions of isolated surface fibers and construct exceptional objects supported on certain fibers.

papers.name: Improved Berezin--Li--Yau Bounds for Dirichlet Eigenvalues via Fourier Coupling and Frequency Concentration
papers.abstract: Let $0<λ_1\leqλ_2\leq\cdots$ be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$. We develop two Fourier-space refinements of the Berezin--Li--Yau argument. For every finite-measure open set, coordinate commutator identities and coupled scalar--vector projections lead to a one-dimensional variational constant $C_n^{\mathrm{new}}$ and the individual bound \[ λ_k\geq C_n^{\mathrm{new}}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{2/n}, \qquad \frac{n}{n+2}<c_n^{\mathrm{env}}<C_n^{\mathrm{new}}<1. \] Here $n/(n+2)$ is the classical Li--Yau individual coefficient and $c_n^{\mathrm{env}}$ is the coefficient associated with the uncoupled scalar envelope developed in our previous paper. Thus the displayed strict hierarchy separates the gain of the scalar energy envelope from the further gain supplied by the commutator coupling. For bounded open sets, a frequency-concentration operator, its first two traces, and the Ky Fan principle force Fourier mass outside the Li--Yau filling ball. A two-region bathtub argument then gives \[ \sum_{j=1}^kλ_j \geq \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω) \frac{n}{n+2}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{1+2/n}, \qquad \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)>1, \] where $\mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)$ is strictly decreasing in $k$ and converges to one, and \[ \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)-1\geq \frac{n+2}{2(n+1)^2} \left(\frac{ω_{n-1}}{ω_n}\right)^2 \left(\frac34\right)^{n-1}k^{-2/n}. \] Thus the sharp leading term in the Berezin--Li--Yau sum is supplemented by an explicit positive, volume-only correction of order $k$. Apart from boundedness in the concentration argument, no boundary regularity, convexity, or connectedness is assumed. These improvements do not prove Pólya's conjecture: the individual coefficient is below one, and the sum multiplier tends to one.

papers.name: Construction of entropies for cross-diffusion systems
papers.abstract: The analysis of cross-diffusion systems with nonsymmetric and indefinite diffusion matrices often relies on the existence of entropies, that is, Lyapunov functionals whose dissipation often yields gradient estimates. We propose a general strategy for constructing entropies for two-species cross-diffusion systems, based on the assumption that the mobility matrix is symmetric, in accordance with Onsager's reciprocal relations. The symmetry condition leads to a linear hyperbolic equation in two variables, which can be reformulated as a linear transport system along the eigendirections of the diffusion matrix, related to the approach of Jenssen and Kogan for hyperbolic conservation laws. Positive solutions to this system yield a family of entropies parametrized by two arbitrary functions of one variable. Sufficient conditions for their existence on (possibly unbounded) characteristic rectangles are given, the mechanisms that may prevent the existence of an entropy are identified, and systems without any entropy structure are presented. The general construction recovers known entropies for models arising in physics and biology and provides new ones. For systems with an arbitrary number of components, we derive sufficient conditions for the existence of separable entropies and give a rank criterion for the uniqueness of entropies (up to affine functions). Cross-diffusion systems without symmetry of the mobility matrix are also discussed.

papers.name: Harper's beyond square-root conjecture for random matrices
papers.abstract: For a Haar unitary matrix $U_N$ of size $N$, we prove that the first absolute moment of $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Sym}^k U_N)$ tends to zero as $\min(N,k)\to\infty$. This settles the random matrix version of Harper's beyond square-root conjecture formulated by Wang and Xu, with no restriction on $k/N$. The proof is elementary and self-contained, combining exact weighted trace moments with a Gaussian change of measure. It also connects the result to the critical chaos model studied by Soundararajan and Zaman, also known as holomorphic multiplicative chaos.

papers.name: Entropy maximization for cube projections
papers.abstract: We prove that, in every dimension $n\ge150$, the one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz in these dimensions.

papers.name: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
papers.abstract: Guérin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory, strongly biased starts are unimodal, and the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval. Outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$, whose uniqueness follows from a positive-weight integral for the central curvature of the fair-start density. We control sign changes in the finite walk's first and second differences, including those created at the boundary, and pass them to the limit. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one.

papers.name: $\mathbb Z$ is diophantine over $\mathbb Q$ with 26 unknowns
papers.abstract: Recently, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. Motivated by this work, G. Conant et al. showed that $\mathbb Z$ is diophantine over $\mathbb Q$, i.e., there is an integer-coefficient polynomial $F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ such that for any $x\in\mathbb Q$ we have $$ x\in\mathbb Z\quad\iff \exists\,y_1,\ldots,y_{n}\in\mathbb Q\ [F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_{n})=0].$$ They constructed such a polynomial $F$ with $°F=4$ and $n=221$.In this paper, we prove the existence of such a polynomial $F$ with $n=26$. We also show that $16$ existential unknowns suffice under the $abc$-conjecture.

papers.name: Rational isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld modules
papers.abstract: We determine the $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-rational points on the Drinfeld modular curves $X_{0}(\mathfrak{n})$ of arbitrary level, obtaining a complete classification of rational cyclic isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules over $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$. As consequences, we prove Schweizer's conjecture on rational torsion, establish optimal uniform bounds on the number of isomorphism classes in an $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-isogeny class of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules and determine the geometric automorphism groups of $X_{0}(\mathfrak{p})$ for primes $\mathfrak{p}$ of degree at least three.

papers.name: GV-subschemes and hyperelliptic Jacobians
papers.abstract: We provide a solution to the hyperelliptic Schottky problem: a principally polarized complex abelian variety whose theta divisor has singular locus of codimension three is a hyperelliptic Jacobian. As a key step towards this criterion for hyperelliptic Jacobians, we prove a conjecture of Pareschi and Popa which predicts that if the ideal sheaf $I_X$ of a subscheme $X$ of an indecomposable PPAV $(A, Θ)$ satisfies that $I_X(2Θ)$ is IT$_0$, then $X$ is a GV-subscheme. As a corollary of the main result, the base scheme of an ample line bundle on a complex abelian variety is generically reduced along every irreducible component of codimension $2$, confirming a conjecture of Debarre. This corollary completes the algebro-geometry proof by Arbarello-Codogni-Pareschi in \cite{ACP21, ACP25} of Novikov's conjecture, which characterizes Jacobians via the KP equation.

papers.name: Toward the abelian category of positive Lagrangians
papers.abstract: We introduce a geometric construction whose terminal configuration determines the kernel and cokernel of a morphism between positive Lagrangian branes in the derived Fukaya category of a Calabi-Yau manifold. Thus, if the construction always terminates, the full subcategory of positive Lagrangian branes is abelian, as conjectured by Joyce. We show that this abelian category admits Harder-Narasimhan filtrations with respect to the central charge defined by the holomorphic volume form. Under appropriate split-generation assumptions, we construct a Bridgeland stability condition whose stable objects are isomorphic to special Lagrangian branes, as predicted by the Thomas-Yau conjecture. The geometric construction is based on a one-parameter family of special Lagrangian submanifolds with boundary. One part of the boundary is contained in the Lagrangian underlying the domain of the morphism and the other in the Lagrangian underlying the codomain. Surgeries occur as the family encounters singularities or obstruction walls. We prove that the construction always terminates for the two-torus and provide higher dimensional examples.

papers.name: $C^{1,α}$ Regularity of $W^{2,2}$ $Q$-Valued Maps with Small Laplacian
papers.abstract: We establish a regularity criterion for $Q$-valued maps $u\in W^{2,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(Ω,\mathcal A_Q(\mathbb R^k))$, where $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$ is open. If $|Δu|\leqδ_*|D^2u|$ almost everywhere, with $δ_*=δ_*(n,k,Q)>0$ sufficiently small, then $u\in C^{1,α}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for some $α=α(n,k,Q)>0$, with quantitative estimates. The result holds for arbitrary $n\geq2$, $k\geq1$, and $Q\geq1$. The proof establishes uniform energy decay using a rigidity principle for positive-semidefinite matrix-valued measures with an aperture bound and approximately atomic divergence, extending the target-stress argument for the homogeneity gap in \cite{Luc26}. The argument relies only on first variation identities. As consequences, we obtain $C^{1,α}$ regularity for Dirichlet-stationary $W^{2,2}$ maps and for locally Lipschitz $W^{2,2}$ maps whose graph varifolds are stationary and have sufficiently small slope. Combining the latter result with Bellettini's Lipschitz sheeting theorem \cite{Bel25}, we establish $C^{1,α}$ sheeting in the multiple-valued sense for two-sided stable minimal immersions whose singular set has vanishing $2$-capacity relative to the immersion, under suitable flatness and mass bounds. Our results allow us to reduce the proof of compactness within this class, under locally uniform mass bounds, to the conjecture that branch sets of stationary $C^{1,α}$ multiple-valued graphs in codimension one have vanishing $2$-capacity.

papers.name: Graded unitarity constraints on simply-laced affine Kac--Moody algebras
papers.abstract: We investigate constraints imposed by four-dimensional unitarity (recently formalised as graded unitarity) on possible simply-laced affine Kac--Moody vertex algebras arising from four dimensions via the SCFT/VOA correspondence. Under the assumption that the $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration is weight-based with respect to the currents and the Casimir operators, with appropriately shifted $R$-charge assignments for the latter, we demonstrate that all values of the level other than a discrete set are incompatible with four-dimensional unitarity. This set includes all the boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, those corresponding to rank-one Kodaira SCFTs, as well as certain non-admissible families conjecturally associated with specific $D^b_q(\mathfrak{g})$ Argyres--Douglas theories. Specialising to $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ with $N$ prime, we find a stronger result: under the same $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration assumption, four-dimensional unitarity rules out all levels except the boundary admissible $k = k_{N,q}$, which are precisely those corresponding to the $D_q^N(\mathfrak{sl}_N)$ Argyres--Douglas theories.

papers.name: Sasakian Hodge Numbers of Calabi-Yau Links
papers.abstract: The link of an isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularity whose degree equals the sum of its weights is a Sasakian manifold that admits a contact Calabi-Yau structure, and its Sasakian Hodge numbers are dimensions of graded pieces of the Milnor algebra of the defining polynomial. In earlier work these numbers were computed with Gröbner bases for the $7$-dimensional links of $7549$ of the $7555$ weighted Calabi-Yau threefold links, and two conjectures were raised from the data. The first asserts that polynomials with the same weights have Milnor algebras whose relevant graded pieces have equal dimensions; the second asserts that the Sasakian Hodge number $h^{2,1}_S$ of the link is bounded above by the Hodge number $h^{2,1}$ of the base Calabi-Yau threefold. Both conjectures are proved here. The first holds for every polynomial with an isolated singularity, because its partial derivatives form a regular sequence; an independent derivation of the Sasakian Hodge numbers by sheaf cohomology on the leaf-space orbifold is also given. For the second, the stringy Hodge numbers of the Calabi-Yau orbifold are shown to bound the middle Sasakian Hodge numbers in every dimension $n\ge2$, and for $n\ge3$ the gap in $h^{n-1,1}$ is shown to be a sum of geometric genera of loci of orbifold points; for threefolds the bound is attained exactly when all curves of orbifold points are rational. The resulting closed formulae give the Sasakian Hodge numbers of the six $7$-dimensional links left open in the earlier work and complete datasets for all $95$ five-dimensional K3 links and all $1\,100\,055$ nine-dimensional Calabi-Yau fourfold links; for the K3 links they recover the previously known second Betti numbers.

papers.name: A new tautological relation on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14}$ in cohomology
papers.abstract: We construct a relation $\mathsf{Q}$ in the cohomological tautological ring $\mathsf{RH}^*(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14})$ which lies outside the space of $3$-spin relations. $\mathsf{Q}$ is a simple linear combination of pure boundary strata classes of codimension 9 supported on the divisor $Δ_0 \subset \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14}$ of irreducible nodal curves, and transforms according to the irreducible representation of $Σ_{14}$ associated to the partition $(2^7)$. The result shows that the set of $3$-spin relations cannot be complete in cohomology. Motivic conjectures relating algebraic cycles to special values of $L$-functions suggest that $\mathsf{Q}$ is nonzero in Chow. More precisely, we prove that the Chow nonvanishing of $\mathsf{Q}$ follows from a conjecture of Harder concerning the failure of the Manin--Drinfeld principle in genus 2. We prove that $\mathsf{Q}$ vanishes in cohomology by pairing with generators of the tautological ring. To prove $\mathsf{Q}$ is not in the set of $3$-spin relations requires an argument involving the $Σ_{14}$-representation-theoretic properties of the $3$-spin relations and the cohomology of local systems on $\mathcal{A}_2$ and $\mathcal{M}_2$. Parallel constructions for other moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$ are discussed in the paper. There are many open questions.

papers.name: On the Hofer-Zehnder conjecture for Reeb flows without symmetry
papers.abstract: This paper continues our investigation of the Hofer-Zehnder conjecture for dynamically convex, non-degenerate Reeb pseudo-rotations of $S^{2n-1}$. The main result of the paper is that, for $n\geq 3$, such a flow has at most $n-3$ alternating prime closed orbits and hence at most $2n-3$ prime closed orbits in total. In particular, the flow on $S^5$ has exactly three prime closed orbits, all of which are non-alternating and elliptic. In addition, we prove that a dynamically convex Reeb pseudo-rotation on a sphere has at least two non-degenerate, irrationally elliptic orbits.

papers.name: The Triangular Abrikosov Constant and the Thomas--Fermi $Γ$-Limit of Rotating Bose--Einstein Condensates
papers.abstract: We resolve the Abrikosov coefficient conjecture for rapidly rotating two-dimensional Bose--Einstein condensates within the variational framework of $Γ$-convergence. For a harmonic trap, we establish the $Γ$-convergence of the rescaled Gross--Pitaevskii energy functionals in the fast-rotation regime, through weak $L^2$ convergence of the rescaled densities, and identify the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with $b_\triangle$, the Abrikosov ratio associated with the triangular vortex lattice. The limiting Thomas--Fermi functional determines the first correction to the minimum energy and the macroscopic density of almost minimizers. For the auxiliary rescaled model and its lowest-Landau-level restriction, we also compute a strictly positive limiting $L^2$ distance between minimizing densities and the Thomas--Fermi profile. The identification of the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with the triangular Abrikosov ratio $b_\triangle$ relies on the sharp Gaussian-minorant theorem established in a recent OpenAI preprint~\cite[Theorem~1.2]{Atomic}. A Fourier representation of the quartic energy and a weighted Poisson identity yield a lower bound for arbitrary magnetic-periodic lowest-Landau-level states. The sign conditions on the minorant and its Fourier transform give the bound, while the lattice contact conditions identify its coefficient with $b_\triangle$. Cutoff and magnetic projection transfer this estimate to local holomorphic states without boundary conditions or periodicity assumptions. Consequently, the free-cell coefficients converge to $b_\triangle$ with error $O(L^{-1/5})$ on squares of side length $L$.

papers.name: A proof of the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture by embedding nilspaces in nilmanifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that every compact finite-rank nilspace admits a continuous injective morphism into a toral nilspace of the same step, and hence into a connected filtered nilmanifold. Combining this embedding theorem with the general nilspace inverse theorem, we establish the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture and extend its conclusion to second-countable compact abelian groups. This yields an inverse theorem for Gowers norms on all such groups, in which the correlating functions factor through morphisms into nilmanifolds. The proof relies on substantial foundations developed in nilspace theory over the past decade, particularly the general nilspace inverse theorem and the representation of compact finite-rank nilspaces as quotients of free nilspaces.

papers.name: Counterexamples to the clamped-plate eigenvalue ratio conjecture
papers.abstract: Ashbaugh in 1999 conjectures that the ball maximizes the ratio of the second to the first eigenvalue for the vibrating clamped-plate problem. We disprove this conjecture by constructing smooth connected domains in every dimension $d\ge2$. The construction starts with an interior sphere on which the displacement is required to vanish. The first two eigenvalues have the same relative increase at first order, but the second increases more at second order. This gives a strict increase of their ratio, which survives approximation of the sphere by finitely many codimension-two supports and their replacement by smooth holes. We identify the limiting Sobolev spaces through trace estimates and logarithmic cutoffs, and use the geometric construction for the buckling problem to obtain connected perforated domains.

papers.name: The Gaps Between the $Δ$-Unknotting Number and Its Lower Bounds
papers.abstract: Let $u^Δ(K)$ denote the $Δ$-unknotting number of a knot $K$, and let $a_2(K)$ denote the second coefficient of the Conway polynomial. It is known that $u^Δ(K)\geq |a_2(K)|$. We define the $Δ$-gap of $K$ by $G^Δ(K):=u^Δ(K)-|a_2(K)|$. In this paper, we investigate the behavior of this invariant for various families of knots. For example, we prove that the $Δ$-gap of the pretzel knot $K=P(2s, 4s-1,4s+1)$, where $s$ is a positive integer, satisfies $G^Δ(K) \geq 4s$. Consequently, the $Δ$-gap is unbounded. To further investigate the structure of the $Δ$-gap, we distinguish between $Δ$-moves that increase $a_2(K)$ and those that decrease it, since each $Δ$-move changes $a_2(K)$ by $\pm1$. We analyze how these two types of moves contribute to the $Δ$-gap. We also investigate the gaps between $u^Δ(K)$ and other knot invariants that provide lower bounds for it. In particular, we establish explicit formulas and lower bounds for these gaps for certain families of pretzel knots, torus knots, two-bridge knots, and Montesinos knots. Our results show that these gaps can be arbitrarily large. In addition, we identify prime positive knots with $u^Δ(K)=2$ or $3$, and propose a conjecture on a lower bound for $u^Δ(K)$ for prime positive knots.

papers.name: Numerical verification for harmonic maps: Counterexamples to Eells' conjecture
papers.abstract: This paper develops a framework to construct harmonic maps $S^3 \rightarrow S^2$ numerically, which is used to construct approximate harmonic maps in homotopy classes with Hopf invariant $2,3,4,5,6$. By using a rigorous fixed-point argument, it is shown that there exist genuine harmonic maps with the same Hopf invariant close to these approximate solutions, thus producing a family of counterexamples to Eells' conjecture, and the related Ding's conjecture.

papers.name: Refined random matrix conjectures for zeros of $p$-adic $L$-functions
papers.abstract: We make and test the conjecture that for $p$-adic $L$-functions associated to quadratic Dirichlet characters and their Teichmüller twists, all local statistics of zeros in the unit disk match those of $p$-adic random matrix eigenvalues. This generalizes the case of the number of zeros in the unit disk previously conjectured by Ellenberg-Jain-Venkatesh, which was well-supported by numerics, as well as the case of the discriminant, where their numerics were more ambiguous. Using recent random matrix results on local statistics of eigenvalues, we make the random matrix prediction explicit for many statistics, analogous to local densities and pair-correlations in the complex setting. To test these, we compute data on $p$-adic $L$-functions for characters of conductor up to $10^7$, and for certain statistics in windows above $10^{10}$. We find good agreement with the new random matrix predictions for these statistics, as well as for the discriminant.

papers.name: The non-stationary $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ affine Laumon function and its difference equation
papers.abstract: We present an explicit $q$-Givental type formula for the $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary affine relativistic Toda or affine Laumon function introduced by Shiraishi. We prove the conjecture of [J. Shiraishi, Affine screening operators, affine Laumon spaces and conjectures concerning non-stationary Ruijsenaars functions. J. of Int. Systems, 4 (2019)], that this function obeys a non-stationary difference equation involving an operator $\widehat{\mathcal T}$, which represents a quiver automorphism (Dehn twist) of the quantum cluster algebra of the affine $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ Q-system.

papers.name: On configurations that are nearly generalised polygons
papers.abstract: Payne (1972) introduced nearly generalised $n$-gons as $(s+1)$-regular bipartite graphs of girth $2n$ with small excess over the Moore bound. Biggs and Ito (1980) proved nonexistence of such graphs if $s > 1$ and $n > 3$, leaving open the existence of regular antipodal planes. We revisit this problem from several equivalent viewpoints. First we show that a regular antipodal plane of order $s$ is equivalent to a balanced weighing matrix whose support is the incidence matrix of a biplane with parameters \[ 2-\left(\frac{s^2+s+2}{2},\,s+1,\,2\right). \] This gives short determinant and local-arithmetic obstructions to existence. We then formulate the question of signing a biplane as an affine linear system over $\mathbb F_2$, and use this formulation to prove that no regular antipodal plane of order $s$ exists with $4\le s\le 14$. Finally, we give further equivalent formulations in terms of sharply deranged families of permutations and mutually orthogonal array-bic squares. These translations provide new computational and structural approaches to Payne's conjecture that regular antipodal planes exist only for $s=2,3$.

papers.name: Ergodicity without monotonicity: patch-positive spin systems
papers.abstract: Monotonicity is the standard tool for proving that an interacting particle system is ergodic. What can replace it when the system is not monotone and its invariant measure is unknown? The simplest such systems are kinetically constrained models such as FA-1f and East exposed to noise. In these models vacancies enable updates, so adding vacancies should help the system forget its initial state. We prove this for a broad class of spin systems, which we call patch-positive. If vacancies are created spontaneously at a uniformly positive rate, the system converges to the same equilibrium from a large class of initial states, and from every initial state if the threshold density is at most $\tfrac12$ or the interactions are oriented. In particular, the East model with noise is ergodic at every density, and we obtain new cases of the positive-rates conjecture. The key idea is to compare the dual processes of the system with and without the added deaths.

papers.name: Higher derived limits, Kurepa families and Chang's Conjecture
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay between homological algebra and combinatorial set theory, specifically focusing on the (non)vanishing of higher derived limits of certain inverse systems of abelian groups, denoted $\mathbf C_{[κ]^λ}$, indexed by the ordered sets $([κ]^λ,\subseteq)$, where $λ< κ$ are infinite cardinals. Our first main result is a general structural theorem which provides a generalisation of Goblot's theorem to the setting of locally small directed sets. We then present the first systematic study of generalised cofinal Kurepa families. We establish their existence in the constructible universe $L$ and under specific cardinal arithmetic hypotheses. Then, we apply our structural result to show that $\mathrm{lim}^{n+2} \mathbf{C}_{[κ]^{\aleph_n}} = 0$ in environments where the appropriate cofinal Kurepa families exist. In contrast, we explore conditions that force these derived limits to be nonzero. In particular, we prove that certain instances of Chang's conjecture (CC), together with the existence of suitable $\diamondsuit$ sequences, imply that $\mathrm{lim}^{n+2} \mathbf{C}_{[κ]^{\aleph_n}} \neq 0$ for appropriate values of $κ$. Adapting forcing techniques from Eskew and Hayut, we construct models of these instances of CC together with the required $\diamondsuit$ sequences, establishing the consistency, for each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, of $\mathrm{lim}^{n+2} \mathbf{C}_{[\aleph_{ω_n}]^{\aleph_n}} \neq 0$.

papers.name: Perfect Matching Complexes of $3\times 2n$ Grid Graph
papers.abstract: The perfect matching complex of a simple graph $G$ is an abstract simplicial complex whose facets (maximal faces) are precisely the perfect matchings of $G$. In this article, we study the topology of the perfect matching complex of the $3\times 2n$ grid graph and show that it is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of $f_{n-1}$ copies of $(n-1)$-dimensional spheres, where $f_{k}$ denotes the $k$-th Fibonacci number. This proves a particular case of the conjecture given by Chandrakar and Singh for perfect matching complex of grid graphs.

papers.name: Upper bounds for the number of spanning forests of a graph
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices, and let $F(G)$ denote the number of spanning forests of $G$. Bencs and Csikvári proved that every $r$-regular graph $G$ with $r\ge 2$ satisfies $F(G)\le r^n$. Motivated by this result, they conjectured that if $G$ has minimum degree at least $3$, then $F(G)\leq \prod_{i=1}^n d_i$, where $(d_1, d_2, \dots, d_n)$ is the degree sequence of $G$. In this paper, we prove that graphs with minimum degree at least $n/3$ $(n\geq7)$ satisfy $F(G)\leq \prod_{i=1}^n d_i$. We also construct a counterexample to the conjecture. We therefore further study the enumeration of spanning forests in general graphs, proving an upper bound in terms of the degree sequence and characterizing the extremal graphs attaining this bound. In addition, using the matrix-forest theorem, we obtain an upper bound for the number of spanning forests of a connected graph in terms of its algebraic connectivity, and characterize the extremal graphs attaining this bound.

papers.name: Sharp Finite-Time Blow-Up for Unforced Axisymmetric Euler Without Swirl via Multiscale Data
papers.abstract: For the unforced Euler equations, we construct a compactly supported initial vorticity within the class of axisymmetric flows without swirl, whose solution blows up in finite time. The initial vorticity belongs simultaneously to every Hölder space $C^α$, $α<1/3$. This is sharp given that global regularity is known when $α=1/3$ in the case of axisymmetric flows without swirl. Previous constructions by Shkoller \cite{Shk26}, Chen \cite{Chen26I,Chen26II}, and Shao--Wei--Zhang--Zhang \cite{SWZZ26} establish blow-up for each prescribed exponent $α$ in the same sharp range. Our construction achieves simultaneous membership in all these spaces. In addition, our construction is short. Our proof uses multiscale initial data, in the spirit of Kim--Jeong~\cite{KJ22}, Córdoba--Martínez-Zoroa--Zheng~\cite{CMZZ25}, and Bang--Cheskidov~\cite{BC26}. The blow-up mechanism is a forward cascade through successively smaller scales. A main difficulty in approaching the critical exponent $1/3$ is caused by large self-deformation. Our main idea to overcome this difficulty is to obtain a lower bound for strain at the stationary non-smooth point by using angular redistribution. A related outstanding open problem is to establish an unforced Euler blow-up from smooth data in the case of axisymmetric flows with swirl. A recent multiscale construction by OpenAI for the unforced Euler equations is, however, non-axisymmetric. Although we work in the no-swirl class, the axisymmetric multiscale mechanism developed here may offer a possible route toward the still-open problem of axisymmetric smooth blow-up.

papers.name: On the periodicity of meromorphic functions of the form $ff^{(k)}$
papers.abstract: For a non-entire meromorphic function $f$ and an integer $k$, we will show that whenever $ff^{(k)}$ is periodic so is $f$. This result gives an affirmative answer to a significant class of the so called generalized Yang's conjecture.

papers.name: Graphs attaining Haemers' toughness bound
papers.abstract: Haemers \cite{Haemers2020} conjectured that every connected noncomplete graph $G$ satisfies $t(G)\geqslantμ_2/(μ_n-δ)$, where $t(G)$ is the toughness of $G$, $μ_2$ and $μ_n$ are its algebraic connectivity and Laplacian spectral radius, and $δ$ is its minimum degree. Greaves and Zhu \cite{GreavesZhu2026} recently proved this conjecture, leaving the equality case open. We characterize all graphs attaining equality: a graph attains equality if and only if its complement has a complete component whose order is at least the Laplacian spectral radius of every other component. Equivalently, its algebraic connectivity and independence number sum to its order. We also determine all vertex cuts attaining the toughness, and show that for regular graphs, the equality graphs are exactly the complete multipartite graphs with parts of equal size.

papers.name: Infinite Index Identities for Argyres-Douglas Theories and Graded Vector Space Isomorphisms for VOAs
papers.abstract: Supersymmetric indices provide stringent tests of dualities between superconformal field theories (SCFTs). We establish infinite families of Schur-index identities among four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ Argyres-Douglas (AD) theories, with the logarithms of their fugacities related linearly. These identities connect theories with markedly different physical properties without requiring infrared duality, while still implying simple relations among their central charges and flavor levels. Through the SCFT/VOA correspondence, they become character identities for the associated affine and $W$-algebras. One broad family relates $D_p(G)$ and $(A_{(h+1)(p-1)},G)$ theories, corresponding to affine and principal $W$-algebras at boundary admissible levels. At the level of the underlying state spaces, these character identities suggest that the corresponding VOAs are related by graded vector space isomorphisms, which are weaker than full VOA isomorphisms. We explicitly construct such a graded isomorphism between the VOAs associated with $(A_1,A_{4p-3})$ and $(A_1,D_{2p})$. We also show the correspondence for universal affine and principal $W$-algebras and test its compatibility with their simple quotients by matching the lowest-degree null states. We establish analogous character identities for certain non-vacuum modules in concrete examples and conjecture a broader extension. Finally, beyond the SCFT/VOA correspondence, we discover similar identities between level-one affine and Virasoro algebras, whose further generalizations point toward a new spectral level-rank duality in WZW models.

papers.name: The Chabauty--Kim dimension inequality via noncommutative Iwasawa theory
papers.abstract: We establish Kim's conjectural dimension inequality for smooth projective geometrically connected curves $C/\mathbb{Q}$ of genus at least two with a rational basepoint. For every odd prime $p$ of good reduction, we prove that $$\mathrm{dim} H_f^1(G_{\mathbb{Q},Σ},U_n^\mathrm{ét}) < \mathrm{dim}(U_n^{\mathrm{dR}}/F^0)$$ for all sufficiently large $n$, where $U_n^\mathrm{ét}$ and $U_n^\mathrm{dR}$ are the $n$'th lower central series truncations of the $\mathbb{Q}_p$-pro-unipotent geometric étale, and de Rham fundamental groups of $C$, and $Σ$ is any finite set of places containing $p$, $\infty$, and the primes of bad reduction. Inspired by Coates and Kim's work on curves with CM Jacobians, we use noncommutative Iwasawa theory to bound second Galois cohomology through dimensions of kernels of certain Iwasawa operators, acting on finite dimensional representations of the ambient generalized symplectic group. We establish bounds for these kernels in terms of the highest weight and dimension of the ambient symplectic representation. No restriction is imposed on the Jacobian's geometric endomorphism ring or its Tate-module Galois image. Consequently, the Chabauty--Kim loci are finite at all sufficiently large levels, recovering the Mordell theorem over $\mathbb{Q}$ through the Chabauty--Kim method.

papers.name: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
papers.abstract: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories. Finally, we conjecture, using the Lazard correspondence, a relation between expectation values of line operators in the two types of theories, and test it in examples.

papers.name: On non-vanishing of the first Hochschild cohomology of blocks
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be a block of a finite group algebra $kG$, where $k$ is an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Inspired by the result of Fleischmann, Janiszczak and Lempken that $\mathrm{HH}^1(kG) \not=0$ when $p$ divides the order of $G$, Linckelmann conjectured that $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)\not= 0$ when $B$ has non-trivial defect. By developing the methods of Briggs, Rubio y Degrassi and the author, we give a fusion theoretic criterion for non-vanishing, proving the conjecture holds for all blocks of abelian defect. Further, we show the criterion holds for all blocks at $p > 5$, proving the conjecture for all such primes

papers.name: Quadratic APN Functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^{10}$ with a Self-Equivalence of Prime Order
papers.abstract: Almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ have the lowest possible differential uniformity. The only known APN permutation in even dimension, in dimension six, is equivalent to a quadratic APN function with a nontrivial linear self-equivalence; no APN permutation is known for even $n \geq 8$. In a published collection of about 3.8 million quadratic APN classes of dimension eight, at most 0.34% have a nontrivial linear self-equivalence. In dimension ten, the 25 literature classes considered here all have one. We study all quadratic APN functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^{10}$ with such a self-equivalence, which usually confines them to a much smaller linear space. Up to conjugacy and power similarity, self-equivalences of prime order have 299 types. We settle 298 of them. Elementary lemmas exclude 280 types, and exhaustive searches confirm this for 242 of them. The other 18 types are settled by exhaustive searches with exact equivalence certificates. Up to extended affine equivalence, the 298 types contain 29 classes of quadratic APN functions, four of them new. This also classifies the quadratic APN functions with coefficients in a subfield. Exactly 24 classes contain one with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_4$, and all 3 that contain one with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_{32}$ are among them. The open type consists of the quadratic canonical triplicate functions. They correspond to maximum additive Hermitian rank-distance codes. Three different searches find only the invariants of 16 classes, all among the 29. We conjecture there are no others. No quadratic APN function in the 298 settled types is Carlet-Charpin-Zinoviev equivalent to a permutation.

papers.name: Color Refinement Distinguishes Connected Rooted Outerplanar Graphs
papers.abstract: Color refinement, also known as the $1$-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm ($1$-WL), is a classical near-linear-time heuristic for graph isomorphism, which also captures the expressive power of message-passing graph neural networks. A long line of work asks on which graph classes $1$-WL, or its higher-dimensional variant $k$-WL, identifies every graph; the least such $k$ is the WL-dimension of the class. Planar graphs have WL-dimension at most $3$ (Kiefer, Ponomarenko and Schweitzer, 2019), and whether $2$-WL already distinguishes all planar graphs is a central open problem. We bring new insight on this question for outerplanar graphs, whose WL-dimension is $2$. We show that color refinement, i.e. 1-WL, distinguishes connected rooted outerplanar graphs: two non-isomorphic such graphs receive different stable colorings once a single vertex, the root, is individualized. The root is necessary, as there are non-isomorphic $2$-connected outerplanar graphs that color refinement does not distinguish. Our result extends to pseudo-rooted graphs, in which the stable coloring merely contains a singleton color class, and to non-connected graphs whose components all contain such a class. Consequently, the $(1,1)$-WL test of Rattan and Seppelt (2023) distinguishes all outerplanar graphs. We proceed by inversion: we reconstruct a connected rooted outerplanar graph, up to isomorphism, from its color graph, the weighted quotient of the graph by its stable color classes, together with its root color. The reconstruction runs in time linear in the output size and is canonical, which yields a near-linear-time canonization algorithm for these graphs. Our main tool is a dichotomy lemma, formalized in Rocq: in a rooted outerplanar graph with an equitable coloring, every block either receives pairwise distinct colors or admits a color-preserving mirror symmetry fixing its vertex closest to the root.

papers.name: Strongly Monotone Central Path Equations for Quadratic Cone Programs
papers.abstract: We introduce a canonical central path for the homogeneous embedding of quadratic cone programs, defined by strongly monotone equations whose modulus is the barrier parameter. We prove that the path exists uniquely, is smooth, and lies on a sphere of fixed radius. Under mild regularity assumptions, its limit points recover optimal solutions or certificates of infeasibility. Exploiting the fact that the embedding operator has a closed-form resolvent, we derive Josephy-Newton steps that retain the nonlinear embedding equations and linearize only the complementarity conditions. Each step reduces to quasi-definite linear system solves and a scalar quadratic. Using this, we derive a new predictor-corrector interior-point method with a surrogate formulation that allows the predictor and corrector to share a single sparse factorization. We provide an open-source implementation, cpo3, for linear and quadratic programs. On 675 instances from eight benchmark collections, with presolve and crossover disabled, cpo3 achieves the highest verified solve count (631) and the lowest penalized shifted geometric mean runtime among the tested open-source and commercial solvers. It is the only tested solver to solve all 138 Maros-Meszaros instances to high accuracy. Moreover, we establish Euclidean and local-norm error bounds that motivate a warm-start heuristic for the proposed algorithm, yielding up to 2.3x median runtime speedup over cold starts on perturbed Netlib and Maros-Meszaros problems.

papers.name: The random KKM mapping principle and its applications
papers.abstract: Based on the recently developed random Brouwer fixed point theorem and the theory of stable compactness, we establish a random Knaster--Kuratowski--Mazurkiewicz (KKM) mapping principle in Hausdorff topological $L^0$-modules. As consequences of this principle, we obtain several results on fixed points, minimax problems, variational inequalities, and conditional games. These results solve a large class of noncompact problems in random functional analysis and its applications.

papers.name: Stability of crystalline measures under random perturbations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study random perturbations and the diffraction properties of translation-bounded crystalline measures. Under a non-vanishing assumption on the known perturbation factor, we prove that, almost surely, any realization of the perturbed measure preserves sufficient structural information to allow the full recovery of the original measure. Previous works have only considered crystalline measures with uniformly discrete supports and equal-mass atoms. Our general setting includes many important crystalline measures that were excluded until now. To treat this broader setting, we adopt a different framework. In this work, we model the perturbation as a random measure rather than as a random set. In particular, this leads us to consider not only perturbations of the support, but also perturbations of the atoms' masses. On the other hand, using elementary techniques of Fourier analysis, we prove that any translation-bounded crystalline measure has a diffraction measure, and we explicitly compute its diffraction.

papers.name: Dynamic Assortment Optimization Under Arbitrary Demand Distributions: The Uniform Price Setting
papers.abstract: We study the joint optimization of assortment and inventory when products are identically priced and the total demand (number of customers) is uncertain. A seller chooses initial inventories before customers arrive and every customer buys her preferred product among those still in stock according to a choice model known to the seller. The objective is to maximize the (expected) total sales, subject to a capacity constraint. We give a $(1-1/e)^2$-approximation under any ranking-based choice model and a $(1-1/e-\varepsilon)$-approximation under the Markov chain choice model, where $\varepsilon$ is a tunable parameter that trades off runtime with approximation guarantee. Our guarantees hold for arbitrary demand distributions and do not require the ubiquitous Increasing Failure Rate (IFR) assumption. In fact, our results also improve on the state-of-the-art approximations for IFR demand distributions. Key to our results is the discovery of hidden submodularity in these problems and the development of efficient procedures to evaluate (or approximate) the objective values. Specifically, we uncover a novel connection to online bipartite matching (for ranking-based models) and use stochastic coupling arguments (for the Markov chain choice model) to reduce the problems to instances of constrained submodular maximization. This opens the door to applying the vast algorithmic machinery for submodular maximization to our problem setting, leading, for example, to natural generalizations beyond cardinality constraint where no approximation results were previously known.

papers.name: Balancing-based model reduction for output-constrained optimal control of switched linear systems
papers.abstract: We develop a balanced-truncation (BT) framework for model-order reduction of optimal control problems governed by switched linear systems, with quadratic tracking costs, convex input constraints, and Moreau--Yosida-regularized output constraints. For general Petrov--Galerkin reduced models, we derive an a posteriori bound for the error in the optimal value function, and combine it with BT-based estimates of the dynamical-system reduction error. We show that BT preserves the duality structure underlying the first-order optimality conditions, making first-reduce-then-optimize and first-optimize-then-reduce equivalent. Consequently, reducing the forward system also reduces the associated optimality system, leading to a certified, online-efficient, and online-adaptive approximation of the parameterized solution operator. The reduced model can therefore be reused across different regularization parameters, constraint sets, switching signals, and reference trajectories.

papers.name: Thresholds of the Polya Szego inequality for the fractional logarithmic p-Laplacian
papers.abstract: We establish three surprising features of the Polya Szego principle for the full signed energy of the fractional logarithmic p-Laplacian. First, the energy doesn't not decrease under rearrangement for all admissible functions. Second, the sharp threshold for Polarization and Schwarz rearrangements are different. Third, for Steiner rearrangement, the threshold in 1 dimension and N dimensions is not the same. Additionally the dimension doesn't appear in the formula.

papers.name: A quotient formula for the Behrend function
papers.abstract: The Behrend function is essential in enumerative geometry. However, computing it, even in zero dimension, has been a highly subtle and mysterious matter since its introduction in the 2000s. We present a quotient formula for the Behrend function of any closed $r$-dimensional affine scheme $X^r \subset \mathbb{A}^N$, evaluated at a singular point, where $0\leq r \leq N-1$. In particular, if the scheme is monomial, we associate parallelepipeds to it and interpret the Behrend function as simple volume information about them. The results here, in particular, recover the recent results of Graffeo-Ricolfi for the zero-dimensional case in 2D in \cite{Graffeo-Ricolfi}, and also the more recent result of Polini-Sammartan-Ulrich on the zero-dimensional case in \cite{PSU26}.

papers.name: Maxwell's equations with thin wires in critical scaling
papers.abstract: We derive effective equations for a situation in which electromagnetic waves hit an array of very thin wires. We study two cases, perfectly conducting wires and highly conducting wires, and investigate in both the critical scaling of the parameters. The electric field $E^η$ and the magnetic field $H^η$ satisfy the time-harmonic Maxwell equations, and the small parameter $η>0$ is the spacing of the wires. A non-critical scaling of the wires implies either that the wires have no effect or that the tangential component of the limiting electric field in the direction of the wires vanishes along the effective interface. In the critical scaling, we observe an interesting effect: The wires act as oscillators and there is a relation between the electric field in longitudinal direction and the jump of the magnetic field in transversal direction involving second derivatives of a flux quantity.

papers.name: Nesting in additive manufacturing using quantum annealing
papers.abstract: Nesting in powder bed fusion (PBF), an additive manufacturing (AM) process, determines the positions and orientations of parts within the build space and influences build height and build time. As the number of parts and feasible placements increases, the nesting problem becomes computationally demanding. Exact approaches are limited to small problem sizes as computational effort increases rapidly with the problem size, while heuristic and metaheuristic approaches involve a trade-off between solution quality and computation time. Quantum annealing (QA) offers an alternative for solving combinatorial optimization problems, but its application to nesting in AM remains largely unexplored. This paper presents a QA-based approach for nesting in AM to investigate its feasibility and its scaling behavior across three problem sizes. An iterative binary quadratic model based approach (IBQM) is developed to minimize build height while considering the geometric characteristics of AM parts. Geometric abstraction, iterative decomposition, and variable pruning are applied to address the computational complexity of the nesting problem. The approach is evaluated using three cases with increasing problem sizes and compared to a classical approach combining tabu search and simulated annealing (TBSA). Compared with TBSA, IBQM reduces the build height of the original parts by up to 13.32% and the computation time by up to 74.27%.

papers.name: Learning observable propagation with sparse local moments
papers.abstract: We propose a unified framework for predicting local moment dynamics in high-dimensional many-body systems from short-time trajectories. Thanks to the locality of the dynamics, we construct the transition moment matrices by projecting the Markov operator onto low-order connected-cluster basis functions supported near the target observable. Exploiting the spatial decay of time-lagged correlations, {these matrices} can be approximated in sparse-plus-low-rank form using trajectory samples, with computational cost scaling linearly in the system dimension and the number of trajectories. The learning error can be further reduced by correcting the memory effect induced by the Galerkin projection. We numerically demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in extrapolating the dynamics of various many-body systems, including Langevin and Glauber dynamics for classical systems as well as Lindblad dynamics for open quantum systems. In addition, for a class of single-site Glauber dynamics, we establish error bounds for sparse-plus-low-rank compression and uniform-in-time bounds for connected-cluster approximation and observable propagation with compressed transition moment matrices.

papers.name: Mesh-Free Weak-Form Regression for Learning Interaction Kernels from Particle Trajectories
papers.abstract: We propose mesh-free weak-form regression for learning interaction kernels from noisy particle trajectories. Our method uses smooth test functions to avoid differentiating noisy data and empirical particle averages to avoid density reconstruction and spatial grids. We then fit sparse combinations of candidate functions, evaluating interaction terms on sampled particle pairs to avoid all-pair quadratic cost. By transferring identifiability from the mean-field limit, we prove high-probability coefficient error bounds that separate finite-particle, time-discretization, observation-noise, and pair-sampling errors, without grid-resolution or density-estimation terms. We evaluate one-dimensional (1D) Newtonian-repulsion, 2D predator-prey, and 10D distance-localized experiments. The numerical results show trends consistent with the theoretical coefficient-error bounds. Comparisons of weak and forward-difference formulations with LASSO, Ridge, and OLS show that weak LASSO gives the smallest coefficient and drift errors in the three nominal experiments.

papers.name: An Obstruction to Realizing Aspherical $3$-Manifold Groups via Torus Surgery
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be a closed, connected, oriented, aspherical $3$-manifold with fundamental group $π= π_1(Y)$ and positive first Betti number $β_1(Y) > 0$, and let $X_0 = Y \times S^1$. We prove that no torus surgery on $X_0$ along a torus-fibered $T^2$-knot $T \subseteq X_0$ can yield a $4$-manifold $X = X_{0; T, f}$ with fundamental group $π$. The obstruction combines the vanishing of the Euler characteristic of $X$ with a classifying-map argument showing that the unimodular intersection form on $H^2(X; \mathbb{Z})$ must admit an isotropic subgroup of rank $β_1(π)$, forcing $χ(X) \geq 2$. Along the way, we also present an independent geometric proof via covering space theory, the Sphere Theorem, and Scott's Core Theorem that the fundamental group of a closed aspherical $3$-manifold is torsion-free.

papers.name: On four problems from the Kourovka Notebook: spectra, periodic automorphism groups, commutators, and operator simplicity
papers.abstract: We examine Problems 18.62(a), 18.63, 18.65, and 20.120 of the Kourovka Notebook. First, a family of semidirect products involving $\operatorname{PSL}_2(p^2)$ gives arbitrarily many pairwise nonisomorphic groups critical with respect to one simple-group spectrum, subject to explicit arithmetic congruences. Second, a completed-algebra construction using sparse torsion identities and a matrix Golod-Shafarevich-Vinberg inequality produces an infinite periodic group generated by two fixed-point-free automorphisms of order five of an abelian group. Third, we give a short matrix proof that the class of elements of order three in $\operatorname{PSL}_2(8)$ contradicts the assertion in Problem 18.65 as written. Finally, we spell out how P. Hall's 1962 wreath-power theorems answer Problem 20.120 under the usual normal-subgroup meaning of simplicity for a group with one distinguished automorphism. The four arguments have substantially different provenance. In particular, the last is a consequence of a known construction, not a priority claim. The two longer constructions are recorded in detail for independent mathematical scrutiny.

papers.name: Score-based neural ordinary differential equations for reaction-diffusions
papers.abstract: A diffusion equation can be rewritten as a transport equation driven by the score function of the evolving density. Conventional probability-flow formulations, which move particles deterministically with this score-driven velocity, typically conserve total mass. In this work, we develop a Lagrangian method for reaction-diffusion equations in which each particle carries a position and a physical weight. The characteristic ODEs incorporate source terms into the evolution of the log-density and its gradient, while particle weights track changes in mass. We combine this representation with a learned velocity field and weighted particle training to approximate these dynamics. For non-increasing reaction rates, a relative-entropy inequality supports the mass-normalized self-consistency residual as the training objective.
